The word trombone derives from Italian tromba (trumpet) and-one (a suffix meaning large), so the name means large trumpet. The trombone has a predominantly cylindrical bore like its valved counterpart the baritone and in contrast to its conical valved counterparts, the euphonium and the horn. The most frequently encountered trombones are the tenor trombone and bass trombone.
